Heh-heh-heh Ehehe, the flowers bloom and fall, Eheho.

Ah, how frustrating, my fate, ah, how frustrating my life.

Once gone, Ehehe, unable to come back, oh ho. 

<When climbing uphill>

@Namu Amita Bul (Buddha's name)']

Name: 4_wedding_bride_bridegroom_marriage
Representative_Docs:
["When the first couple joined together,  
In Eden's flowery garden decided,  
No festive toast yet echoed around,  
For see, it had no dining companions.  
But the feathered creatures did not remain silent,  
And came to crown that marriage with praise,  
Yes, they sang a striking wedding song,  
To show joy to the jubilant couple. (repeat)

The field was the green wedding feast,  
On which no cook displayed his art,  
There was no roast nor fish to be found,  
But the tasty fruit from woods and valleys.  
Clear water flowed instead of wine,  
Yet love might crown the celebration.  
One can be joyful with little,  
If love and joy inhabit the heart. (repeat)

Praise still be to these later times,  
Now we see the table adorned with taste,  
Sometimes one is so greatly delighted,  
When a large company may celebrate.  
Though Adam might crown his marriage  
With sips of mild water,  
We prefer to use grape juice,  
To show the marrying couple more joy. (repeat)

You then, who are paired today,  
We wish to toast in your honor,  
Your wine will not be spared by us,  
It is to drink to your health.  
If love already makes you happy,  
May friendship also inhabit your heart,  
We bring you this cup of wine,  
To show you our friendship. (repeat)", 'Come, now clear from the chest  
Our festive song must sound,  
But singing brings thirst,  
Singers must drink.  
Fill the glass to the brim,  
Then it is indeed at hand,  
See what a lovely little shine, ) repeat.  
It is a lovely little wine. ) repeat.  
Everyone take part in the joyful song;  
Join the chorus,  
Let us not keep our joy silent!  
Let the neighbors hear it,  
How on this happy celebration,  
Forgetful of worries, we are joyful,  
Let the festive song rise, ) repeat.  
No one may be silent here. ) repeat.  
Hail to you, Bride! Health and joy  
We wish you from the heart,  
All that gladdens your heart,  
Never yield to sorrow.

Taste what increases your happiness,  
Always taste with your spouse,  
Prosperity everywhere, ) repeat.  
Joy, health, and blessing. ) repeat.  
Hail to you, Groom! at all times  
May your fortune increase,  
May sorrow silently pass your door,  
May it turn its back on you;  
Misfortune remain always strange to you,  
In all that you undertake,  
Then you both can always, ) repeat.  
Delight in your fate. ) repeat.  
Then rejoice, Friends! joyful in spirit,  
Let the sound of rejoicing be heard,  
At the pleasant wedding celebration,  
May the joy be pleasing.  
Blend the clinking of the cups,  
Joining in friendship,  
Then raise the glass, ) repeat.  
May the Bridal Couple live. ) repeat.', 'The day of the joyous celebration is here,  
The joy sounds loudly,  
In honor of this worthy couple,  
Adorned with silver crowns.  
Raise your song, o friends!  
Sing merrily, again and again,  
So that your cheerful festivity  
Sounds in honor of the Silver Pair. (repeat)  

The groom, esteemed for his virtue,  
As well as his worthy bride,  
They receive our best wishes,  
With lively accompaniment;  
Yes, certainly upon the generous reception,  
They are now welcome here,  
As they proudly appear once again  
As bride and groom. (repeat)  

How many honest and virtuous pledges  
Adorn your marriage crown,  
And contribute to the joy of the bond,  
Your marriage as a reward;  

Their grateful heart is devoted to you,  
So noble for your virtue,  
Behold how that heart is now delighted,  
And rejoices in your happiness. (repeat)  

May you both live long, blessed with well-being,  
Finding gentle cause for joy,  
Let this joyous celebration be for you a symbol,  
Of the marriage’s flower garden;  
Proceed together with a clear mind,  
To many more years,  
And celebrate once the Golden wedding,  
As joyfully as this hour. (repeat)  

O marital love! O highest joy,  
That delights the human heart,  
O friendship! pure soul’s delight,  
To you both our song honors;  
Weave mirth and palm into a victory crown,  
Share your influence with us,  
For you resound the happiest tone,  
At the universal hurrah! (repeat)']

Name: 5_salvation_praise honor_prayer_virtue
Representative_Docs:
['Dear great God, how have You been dishonored,
By unrestrained, human kind,
For Your name is being
Heavily slandered and brought to disgrace because of our sins;
Oh! what greater evil does one see on many ships,
Where evil is eagerly embraced,
And where everyone,
As if a virtue, drags it forward with joy.
What greater evil does one hear being mentioned,
Slandering and cursing, has become very common;
Many want to repay evil with evil,
Or their mouth is full of light songs,
Of lewd talk, and of drunkenness,
And of venomous gossip,
In this wicked attempt,
Everyone seeks the highest ranks.
Much of their talk is full of horror,
Many must hear much lewdness,
Sometimes they mock the prayers,
Yes, they grieve over it when it is done,
For it is too long to be at Prayer for even a small half hour, oh wicked custom!
Where at the revelry,
One could last a whole day.
Brothers, do you not think if you dishonor God the Lord
Like this, that He will also,
(According to your deserts) torment you with punishment,
In the comfortless sad valley of tears,
Where a bitter woe, with gnashing of teeth,
The evil people will strike most severely,
In the hellish kingdom,
Where it will burn eternally.
But this is not said to you all,
As if God’s names are by everyone
Thus godlessly and slanderously with blasphemies
Dishonored and trampled underfoot,
For there are many who greatly dislike this,
And (for the love of God) complain about it
Serving the Lord,
And also uphold His honor.
But this is said to the open,
Worldly servants, who (as if it were a virtue)
With their tongue continually slander the Lord of Hosts,
With pleasure, and joy,
And with shameless cursing, and horrid swearing,
They go about dishonoring Him most grievously,
And whose heart, stubborn and
Does not turn away from this wicked deed.
Yet I pray you all, flee such works,
Take heed to God’s Word,
Keep His Law,
Serve Him as He teaches you in His Churches,
Turn away from evil, and pursue good,
Then God will also protect and guard you,
From the violence of the waves
In your journey,
Storms, and sorrow
Will then not burden you.
If you serve Him thus, and evil comes your way,
Then His mercy will abundantly
Be your help, He will not abandon you,
If you cry to Him in distress,
But He will then hear your brief prayer,
And you shall never be lost,
For God has sworn
This covenant through the mouth of His Prophet.
He will give you comfort and help in your pressure
So that you shall not perish through it,
And over that He will, after this life,
Forgive you all your debts out of grace,
And when you come to die,
You shall obtain the throne of Heaven
Through His good favor!
And His glorious kingdom
You shall also graciously inherit.', '1.  
The Christian’s highest duty,  
Of which God’s word speaks,  
Can never be more perfect,  
Than that they steadfastly  
Sharpen the mind  
To do good,  
To fear God earnestly.

2.  
Is it always good, even more so,  
Now since the Lord  
Enriches your years anew,  
That you are mindful  
That with this new time,  
New virtue must also accompany.

3.  
This is my wish and prayer,  
That soul’s and body’s pain  
Never disturb your rest here,  
Which you find in God; and especially,  
If through the Spirit,  
You are reborn in every way.

4.  
No one is moved to this,  
But death of earthly lease,  
And anything that the flesh desires:  
Unless one violently  
Suppresses the flesh’s passions,  
The spirit here never truly rests.

5.  
Seek the heavenly, the earthly perishes,  
Learn to die before you die,  
So that when the hour of death  
Suddenly comes upon you,  
You do not then learn to refuse the evil,  
(that now is the time).

6.  
Flee foolish pride,  
And foolish vanity:  
Much rather be present  
In spirit, and go inward,  
For inner adornment  
Is precious in God’s eyes.

7.  
Never let unfruitful words  
Depart from your lips,  
They offend pious ears:  
But produce all that has edification,  
So that it gives  
Grace to those who hear it.

8.  
Narrow is the path of life,  
Nothing unclean has hold there:  
So do not seek space where it is narrow:  
God’s word is easily misinterpreted  
According to the flesh’s convenience:  
Whereby one becomes slow and lukewarm.

9.  
Is it then sinful  
To act joyfully?  
Oh no, I would not say that:  
Yet I find it necessary  
That joy originates,  
From God, I return to Him.

10.  
Now that the Spirit lives,  
Strive to celebrate the best,  
Endeavor to imitate Christ,  
So you are refreshed in Him,  
And keep watch for His coming,  
You will find heaven on earth.

11.  
Oh, sweet slavery!  
Who is freer?  
Than one who is bowed before God,  
Enjoys Him here in hope,  
Sees the freedom to come,  
With spiritual eyes.

12.  
This I now wish for you,  
That you grow weary of the world,  
Desire only God:  
And withdraw your mind  
From earthly goods,  
And for God, lack everything.

13.  
Ah Lord! grant that we  
May continuously lift up  
Our hearts and eyes to You;  
And watch in the Spirit,  
To be with You here and especially  
To enjoy You hereafter.', "1.  
What is His Majesty of Heaven,  
Just in His deeds,  
Who punishes rebellion in its time,  
To all those who dare  
To undertake their boldness for evil;  
And who rise against His Power,  
Which He has given in this life:  
To the Authority.  

2.  
To carry ourselves respectfully  
According to their high counsel;  
And never oppose the helm of state,  
But to carry out their will diligently,  
Before the sword has trained them;  
Out of rage from its sheath:  
In anger spreading upon us.  

3.  
As recently happened on the land's ship Venus,  
To mutineers who surely,  
Regretted their crimes;  
Which they had committed boldly,  
In large numbers undertaking,  
Threatening their souls  
With powder, as if to destroy.  

4.  
And causing the ship to explode in the air!  
If the tyranny,  
Of their vain desire!  
Did not go according to their wish,  
Which with much gentleness,  
After a very long time  
They continually confessed,  
Was soon quickly breached.  

5.  
His Highness then gave the order  
To attack them;  
Fiercely besieged a war council:  
Of captains and lords,  
Of the High Admiralty;  
So that through wise policy,  
By their council's decisions,  
These atrocities could be stopped.  

6.  
Kinsbergen, a brave knight,  
In all matters of sea power,  
Denied their intentions,  
By his very diligent watchfulness,  
Which he did day and night,  
And was very close upon them,  
To compel by his power  
If they committed anything.  

7.  
Everyone performed this brave deed,  
Clearly as if shaking,  
So that all the people rose,  
In fear that they also might suffer:  
This hero with his ship's crew;  
If this evil turned worse,  
Their plan would come  
Which did not deter them at all.  

8.  
Shortly thereafter, a writer was sent  
By the war council;  
To the rebels; who however wicked,  
Stood in their orders,  
Were received with leniency,  
And were courageously read a letter from His Highness,  
Which brought them to fear.  

9.  
In which His Highness promised them:  
To show his favor,  
If their supreme leader  
Would respectfully be restored;  
And granted pardon to the sailors,  
So that they might be distributed aboard the surrounding ships,  
And continue in their service.  

10.  
But the non-commissioned officers,  
At the war council, as desired,  
Had to appear as required,  
To show them in all honor,  
With respect,  
Why they committed this bold behavior:  
As if they undertook it  
And came to do so.  

11.  
Not even twenty-four hours were given  
For their deliberation;  
To then willingly,  
Without resistance,  
Obey their command,  
Without any further delay,  
To conduct themselves accordingly,  
Either as pleased.  

12.  
By harsh means, however severe,  
To compel them for their sin;  
So that in time to avoid danger,  
They might not be surrounded,  
They had to be inclined to  
Give their lawful sovereign  
The reason why  
They behaved thus.  

13.  
They sent in response  
By a letter to be known,  
That everything would be as required,  
Forgiven and forgotten;  
But that they might again have:  
Their officers, as requested,  
Aboard, to remain faithful in service.  

14.  
Whereupon a lord vice-admiral,  
Answered them again,  
That they disturbed neither themselves  
Nor any story however named,  
And accepted no conditions,  
But that the wise counsel  
Was to be done with His Highness;  
According to what his power commanded.  

15.  
After a little time of deliberation,  
They further resolved  
To honor the deed  
Of His Highness’s will,  
Whereupon a signal was given  
To all the ships at anchor,  
Which spread on all sides,  
By boats.  

16.  
And so together aboard,  
They came to fetch them away,  
The non-commissioned officers,  
Felt and, without hesitation,  
Were placed on various ships;  
And the people who had been pardoned,  
Given their freedom,  
The rest remained on the ship.  

17.  
Now those who are guilty stand  
To receive their punishments,  
Who rose against their sovereign  
Through their evil ways,  
Yet God who governs the universe  
Here on earth,  
Gives each reward according to their deeds,  
As can be observed here.  

18.  
The war council, shortly thereafter,  
Sentenced three of the most severe rebels  
To be slain by a bullet there!  
The corporal, boatswain, gunner,  
Were the foremost among them,  
To whom this was read,  
But praised for their mercy.  

19.  
By His Highness’s humanity;  
This matter was alleviated.  
Before the punishment at the time,  
Had been carried out on them,  
So that with thrice beating with the cane,  
And whipping, would suffice;  
Their wicked atrocities  
Boldly confessed.  

20.  
Thus the others were also  
Punished for misdeeds,  
Keep God in mind and in peace,  
When He in His mercy,  
Sees all this to each one,  
To not fall into weeping  
From punishments in judgment,  
Before which no one can acquit themselves."]

Name: 6_sailors_sailing_sail_set sail
Representative_Docs:
["Who wants to hear a New Song
Exalted from our Fishermen,
Listen well to my message,
Those who venture on the North Sea,
Without fear or trembling,
With brave courage,
And stake their lives,
In God's keeping,
On the open Sea,
To do each according to his diligence
And very gladly,
Return home.
Friends, our Ship is already prepared,
If God will but give a good Wind,
We sail all guided by God,
Uplifted in our trade,
To live together,
Holy according to God's Word,
As it may please,
Always forward and onward,
To God's delight
With courage always,
To do our diligence,
Our days of life.
Farewell now, dear Friends,
Who inhabit our City,
We commend you all to God,
Young and old People,
As we now part,
For a short time,
May the Lord lead you,
And bless you with health;
Farewell Father and
Mother,
Sisters and Brothers all,
Trust indeed,
In God our Keeper.
We sail all in good spirits,
With a good Wind uplifted,
We hope in God's keeping,
To set out for that purpose,
Like the honorable Apostles,
Together following Christ's words,
To Fish on the Sea,
As they have done,
According to Matthew's teaching,
Casting the Net to the right side,
With Peter joyfully,
On the Word of the Lord.
When we come to the northern Sand,
We shoot our Herring-net,
We then put it in God's hand,
To enjoy the Herring,
Listen to my testimony,
We get a good Catch,
We shoot with pleasure,
Our Corner-net quickly,
Without delay,
Each doing his diligence,
With glad courage,
To our liking.
If we get a good catch of Fish,
Then we rejoice,
We thank the Lord for sure,
And put pressure aside,
Without long hesitation,
If they then drop anchor,
Then we prepare ourselves,
With a very cheerful heart,
To sleep a while,
And that does not last very long,
We move along,
Again with the Boys.
Thus we continue our Trade,
Until the Voyage ends,
We live according to God's Holy Word,
May He send us His blessing,
But if we do otherwise,
God will withdraw His hand,
And His gentle blessing,
From us for
He will reveal
Whoever acts against His will,
It is not good,
To sail this way.
If we get Storm and also Thunder,
As often happens,
Protect us then,
O good Lord:
That no one regrets it,
In the great Sea distress,
Punish, the Waves ward off,
So that we do not as dead,
Discouraged Hearts stand,
But strengthen us,
As your good Disciples,
In the Sea-flood
They could endure.
When God then calms the Waves again,
And brings good Weather,
Very soon we take our turn,
With joy taken out
To our Trade once more,
With a peaceful life,
Until we return,
Again to reckon,
To our Friends in the Dutch valley,
With joyful cheer,
Come together.
When we then come ashore again,
With abundant blessing,
Everyone offers us their hand,
Speak kindheartedly,
Be welcome Friend with peace,
And honorable Ladies,
Do the same likewise,
To their Husbands truly,
The kind Parents,
To their Children at this time
Welcome joyfully,
They quickly shout.
Farewell then all you Fishermen together,
Who cultivate the North Sea,
I commend you in God's name,
Always trust in Him,
He will help you well,
Out of every heavy need,
Stay the Flood surely,
Although He makes a great clamor,
Without wavering
Always firmly hold to His Doctrine,
Then the Lord sends
His rich blessing.
Who first sang us this little Song,
It was a young man done,
Out of love for many young Fishermen,
He went to present this,
Sail well now uplifted,
You all Fishermen,
On the North Sea written,
I tell you truly,
The Year Sixteen Hundred,
And six times ten capable,
Farewell all together,
None excluded.", 'There, the journey is done;
The Prize costs us dearly.
It went terribly;
It was nothing but blood, and fire,
And smoke, and dreadful shouting:
What a guest we became!
But just so you know, the brave sailor
Also took some hits!
The Captain led us constantly,
In the heat of the fight,
We all flew in his footsteps;
Just as the man says.
Everything really went well:
And if it had to be this way,
Not a day were we at sea,
When look, a Brigantine,
Came boldly towards us;
How happy we were then!
Although it gave us full force,
We held firm;
And gave back as well as we could.
The bullets whizzed by;
They beat fiercely on the drum
By them, and on our board.

What did we have standing?
Our rudder was theirs.
We shouted: "Long live the Fatherland,
The Devil take the Brit."
They shouted nothing but: dam you, dam!
Dutch Devils! bless the King.
And I hardly know how it happened
That I sustained a wound,
Somewhere at the side of my neck;
The blood dripped long on my vest:
Well, tin box, how faint I grew!
And Flipmaat got the rest.

He fell dead as a doornail, that good fellow.
Well, that's how it was! See there,
His bravery is known to us,
It troubled us all:
But, come, he died on the bed of honor,
As the proverb goes:
A brave Sailor asks for no more.
Once we all must get out.
But it worries me terribly about his wife;
Who knows how she suffers!
There she sits with a child four or five;
She has lost her husband after all.

We still have many wounded;
But only Flip is dead.
The Brigantine got its share
Of bullets, powder, and scrap.
Then we all boarded,
Like Lions at board;
My wound did not stop me there,
I just kept on.
They then risked one chance,
We became somewhat wiser!
And so we ended that dance:
"Hooray! The ship is Prize."
We were in no good mood;
We received bad news:
How gladly would we have fought
In the hold again over news!
I gave one such a good hit,
He crashed against the deck.
And if mate Hein had not prevented it,
I would have given him more on his face!
What did he have
To curse at a sailor?
Is fighting not free for us too?
Look, I was furious angry.

Then the Captain gave a new order
That no one should harm them:
The man undoubtedly meant well,
Although I regretted it at the time.
But, while I walk up and down,
And fly front and back,
I see a Pea Coat in the crowd,
Who, if I am not mistaken,
Is my old faithful schoolmate.
And it was just right;
I called to him: "Were you there, Kris?
That went well."

"For sure!" he shouted, "now that's good,
The Prize is well deserved;
The Zeeland privateer fought fiercely!"
"But what are you doing here, friend?"
I asked again. "Say, what happened?
You were such a good man;
But if you side with the Englishman,
Then just stay where you are."
"Hey, do you dare ask me that again?"
He shouted; "I am enlightened!
But know, I am a man of honor,

['The husband went to the ice house, the father-in-law went to give thanks.  
After visiting both the ice house and the thanksgiving ceremony, they were told to fill the backyard field.  
They gave a hoe, but the woman had no sack to carry it.  
Though everyone else left for lunch, this lunch never came out.  
When they went inside the house,  
The father-in-law said, "Oh dear, is that really work?"  
Looking for lunch, looking for the day,  
The mother-in-law said, "Oh dear, is that really work?"  
Looking for lunch, looking for the day,  
The sister-in-law, with a ladle,  
Hit the ground with a hoe, saying, "Make it go this way or that way."  
"Is that really work?"  
"Looking for lunch, looking for the day."  
When going to the husband, the cotton tree had cotton bolls,  
A string of them hung here and there; the big cotton tree had big cotton bolls,  
A string of them hung here and there;  
The new straw hat had a brim,  
The paulownia tree flower filling the village,  
Delivered the brightness like it could be seen,  
When pushing away the big cotton tree’s big cotton bolls,  
There was a towel three feet long.  
“Go, go, am I going?”  
They gave rice,  
Rice from an old three-year-old pot,  
A spoonful of rice was thrown ten li away,  
They gave a spoon to eat,  
But only a spoon without a handle was given,  
“Go, go, am I flying as a fly?”  
Returning after one round,  
The girl’s child was trembling,  
After another round,  
The little girl came out,  
“Little girl, little girl, please cut my hair, please cut my hair,  
Cut this hair,  
They cut it and yet didn’t cut much,  
Am I the only one here?  
I have no one to look for me.”  
“Please cut my hair, please cut my hair.”  
After having her single braid cut,  
Unstoppable tears fell like rain,  
“Oh little girl, let’s go begging,  
Let’s go begging at my parental home,  
Going to my parental home to beg,  
My mother said,  
‘Our daughter’s voice is female,’  
Honey, honey, wandering around all the alleys,  
The same person has come out.”  
“Hello, hello,”  
They said harsh words,  
“I don’t want harsh words,”  
They said sticky words,  
“I don’t want sticky words,”  
“Please give sticky words.”  
Giving sticky words,  
They brought a bottomless sack,  
When poured, it all spilled out,  
“Oh, how frustrating, little girl,”  
They asked for a broom,  
But didn’t want even a broom,  
Tonight,  
Tonight once more,  
They went gently and departed.  
“Friend, friend, let’s go begging to our in-laws,  
Going to the in-laws to beg,  
The sesame field has become,”  
“In front of my husband, big flowers have bloomed,  
In front of the sister-in-law, little shamrock flowers have bloomed,  
In front of the brother-in-law, rain flowers and uddu flowers have bloomed,  
In front of my husband, big flowers have bloomed,  
The rice was cut cleanly; next to me, the friend  
Bent the skirt hem, the skirt string broke off,  
And became a white butterfly.”', 'Three days after getting married, I was told to go weed the millet field.  
Going to weed the millet field, I found the field was as hard as stone,  
The field I was to weed was as hard as rice husks.  
I weeded one row, then two rows,  
After three or four hours of helping,  
Even though lunch was served,  
Our lunch was not brought out.  
When I went back inside the house,  
The love door (room to the in-laws) was slammed open,  
And my father-in-law said,  
"Hey, hey, daughter-in-law, how many rows did you weed in the millet field?  
Weed one row, then two rows,  
Then three or four rows again."  
"Hey, woman, go away!  
Do you call that weeding?"  
When lunch was served,  
The door to the main room was slammed open,  
And my mother-in-law said,  
"Hey, hey, daughter-in-law, how many rows did you weed in the millet field?  
Weed one row, then two rows,  
Then three rows repeatedly."  
"Hey, woman, shoo away!  
Do you call that weeding?"  
When lunch was served,  
I went into my room,  
Spread out nine panels of eaves,  
Made a hat with one panel,  
A scarf with two panels,  
A basket with four panels,  
And then I went to visit my parental home.  
Turning one corner,  
The district chief was standing there,  
"District chief, district chief, please shave my head,"  
After shaving one corner,  
Tears welled up in my eyes,  
After shaving two corners,  
Tears streamed down,  
After shaving front and back hair,  
I cried and cried.  
On that path, I arrived at my parental home,  
"Please lend me some millet,"  
Falling on the millet floor, I spilled all over the ground.  
My mother said,  
"Use the broom to sweep it away,"  
"Break the millet stalks and eat them,"  
But I am not the kind of person who eats from the tip of a broom or a millet stalk.  
"Let's eat dinner till sunset,"  
My mother said,  
"The Bodhisattva will bless us with offerings and dinner,"  
"There are cows in the stable and dogs under the floor,"  
I fell asleep in the feedroom,  
The moon was bright and the stars were bright.  
My mother said,  
"Seeing the bright moon and stars,  
You should be able to see the piece of phoenix wood,  
But if you want to see the phoenix piece,  
Look around the feedroom."  
Looking around the feedroom,  
"Child, you came?"  
They cried sadly.  
After explaining everything,  
Compassion arose naturally,  
I lived there for three or four years,  
And then went to my married home.  
At my mother-in-law's grave, chrysanthemums bloomed,  
At my father-in-law's grave, forsythias bloomed,  
At my husband's grave, hibiscus flowers waved gently in the wind.

- Folklore lyrics', 'Three days after getting married, what my mother-in-law said:

Where have you been, my daughter-in-law? Where have you been, my daughter-in-law?  
Do you want to weed the field or the rice paddy? The field need not be weeded,  
but how can the rice paddy be weeded? She said, "Follow the dog."  
So I followed the dog and found it had gone to the field.  
Weeding one row, then two rows,  
my finger that once wore a silver ring,  
why now is it tied with hemp string?  
The silk apron I once wore,  
why now is it a cotton apron?  
The floral shoes I used to wear,  
why now are they woven from straw?  
When I looked around carefully,  
as evening came,  
no matter how many rows I weeded—one row, two rows, three rows—  
all other hearts may have come out,  
but my heart does not come out.  

When I went inside the house,  
the front and middle doors were all locked.  
"Sister-in-law, open the door!  
I’ve been weeding the fields," I said.  
In the scorching sun of a cold day,  
no matter how many rows I weeded—one row, two rows, three rows—  
all other hearts may have come out,  
but my heart does not come out.  

"Go away, you wretched woman!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you looking for the right time and day?"  
This is what my father-in-law said.  

"Go away, you wretched woman!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you looking for the right time and day?"  
My mother-in-law said sharply:  
"Go rot away in your own house!  
Is this what you call work?  
Are you waiting for the right day and time?"  

Crossing the southern hill with determination,  
she dipped the rice she ate the night before  
into a bowl of soup,  
and wiped the crumbs of three years’ worth of meals  
onto a small dish.  
Feeling sorry and downhearted,  
she ate those all up,  
then entered my room.  

She took nine pieces of the widow’s dress—  
carefully unfolded each layer—  
one piece was torn,  
one piece was shaped into a cone,  
one piece was finely cut,  
and when one roll was spun round and round,  
my husband who had gone to Seoul came down  
wearing a hat like the heavens,  
riding a horse above the attic,  
and dismounting with a bang.  

Startled, I said:  
“Hold my wrists tightly,  
hey, you! Hey, you!  
Where are you going? Where are you going?  
I can’t live anymore,  
I can’t live in your house.  
Your parents are frightening,  
your younger siblings are frightening.  
Their parents always demand 'buy me',  
and your siblings also keep demanding 'buy me'.  
Come with me, come with me!  
I just can’t live here, I just can’t live here!”  

When one turn of the roll went by,  
a friend came out and called,  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
cut my hair, please.”  
After she cut one side of my hair,  
the dew started to fall naturally,  
after shaving the double braids,  
a great wailing naturally arose.  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
let’s go begging at my maternal home.”  

Entering the gate of my parental home,  
“Please give me alms, please give me alms.”  
My eldest son-in-law cursed,  
“Among these people, some look like our sister-in-law.”  
“I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike.”  
“Should I give you glutinous rice liquor or non-glutinous rice liquor?  
I throw away the glutinous and non-glutinous rice,  
please give me millet.”  
I gather millet endlessly in a bottomless pit until sunset.  

My sibling, going to the village school,  
said, “Among these people, some resemble our elder sister.”  
“I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike.”  
My mother is ill,  
and some resemble my daughter.  
"I’ve traveled north, south, east, and west,  
many look alike."  

As the day ended,  
I thought I’d stay a while in this house,  
but there was no room, so I couldn’t sleep.  
Trying to sleep under the floor,  
I sat there but couldn’t sleep because worries came flooding.  
It was almost midnight.  

“Mother, mother, my mother,  
I didn't realize this was how it would be.”  
I repeatedly knocked on the three doors,  
when my mother opened the door,  
she cursed loudly,  
and clasping both hands together,  
she wailed loudly.  

As day broke,  
I went around with my friend,  
traveling north, south, east, and west.  
“Friend, friend, my friend,  
let’s go begging at my marital home.”  

When I went begging at my marital home,  
at my father-in-law’s grave, the dragon’s spirit flower bloomed,  
at my mother-in-law’s grave, the wild grass flower bloomed,  
and at my husband’s grave, the hibiscus flower bloomed.  

Looking around my house,  
the hemp field had become untended.  
“Let me split it, let me split it,  
hey, you! Hey, you!  
Let me split just half,  
let’s try living in the afterlife.”  
When splitting half,  
he entered that grave.']

['Once I traveled to Turkey,  
A bit to Narva land,  
Half a mile to Poland,  
I didn’t see the wonder,  
That I saw in my village,  
In my Otsaje household:  
Bulls were barking, dogs were plowing,  
The sheep went to the barn to lay eggs,  
The hen brought two lambs,  
The cow brought a calf of the meadow.  
The horse was a bull-calf,  
The girls were making weddings,  
The women were chopping wheel wood,  
The men were walking the tavern road.', 'I traveled a bit in Turkey  
A hundred versts in Germany,  
A little on the road to Narva  
Half a verst in Finland.  
I did not see the wonder  
That I saw in Näo village.  
Bulls were barking, dogs were plowing,  
Cats were weaving fabric.  
The pig went to work, the sickle was on the belt,  
The fox traveled with reins around its neck.  
The horse brought a young bull calf,  
The cow brought a clump of grass,  
The sheep went to the table to lay eggs.  
The hen brought two lambs,  
Girls made sledges,  
Women spun spinning wheels,  
Men walked the path of straws.', 'I traveled a bit in Turkey,  
A hundred versts in Germany,  
A little on the Narva road,  
Half a verst in Poland.  
I have never seen the miracle  
That I saw in Näuküla:  
Bulls were barking, dogs were plowing,  
Cats were weaving cloth,  
The pig went to work, the sickle was at its waist,  
The fox stood with reins around its neck.  
The horse brought a bull-calf,  
The cow brought a little washbasin,  
The sheep went to lay eggs in the barn,  
The hen brought two lambs.  
Girls were busy spinning,  
Women were carding wool,  
Men were walking the tavern road.']

Name: 26_catch fish_fishing_fish_fish caught
Representative_Docs:
['Amidst the vast, endless waves,  
Seagulls fly into the Red Island bay among a hundred people,  
The wild geese of the upper river fall as soldiers.  
Eya-cha, eya, is it you, long, slender reeds?  
Strongly guarded, the funerals know nothing of the eternal river—  
The noble farming is only called impure.  
Eya-cha, ah, where have the seagulls gone?  
Do they not know the changing tide? Where have the boatmen gone?  
Do they not know the boat has departed? Eya-cha.  

Looking at human life, whenever we live in this world,  
If we want to fish, the fish caught in the East Sea  
eat the young and become juveniles,  
Fish from the South Sea grow old and become squid,  
Fish from the West Sea grow old and become conger eels,  
Fish from the North Sea, pollock, grow old and become frozen pollock.  
Ehe, ehya, when passing through this place, twelve of our sailors,  
with bright winds and fresh breezes, anchor at the edge of the seaweed patch,  
and dance slowly, saying "Let’s quickly return to our hometown,  
build a three-room, six-foot house, care for our parents,  
and live for a thousand, ten thousand years."  
Eya diya, ehe ehe.  

Looking at this world, maidens grow old and become grandmothers,  
Bachelors grow old and become elders, oh gee-yah.  
Looking once more at this world, Daecheon is the Red Island,  
The moon rising over the peach mountain is the tears of Zhuge Liang,  
The spring breeze melody in the silver water is the sorrow of Emperor Wu of Han,  
Do not boast of your pride and arrogance in the bathhouse.  
When our lives grow old, when will we ever return again?  
Eya diya, eheya, oh gee-yah-cha diya-cha.  

Listen, adults, pull together, push forward,  
Oya diya, iya iya.  
If you speak of spring breeze in all matters, peace and stability in the kingdom is the best.  
Millionaires, do not boast, even a small thatched house is enough.  
Peaceful and prosperous times are the best.  
Eoya diya diyeo.', 'The life of the sea folk is,
As they, full of tempests.
When their fish is caught,
They bring it into the towns.
When they also go out fishing,
They must endure many storms,
Before the little Pentecost returns.

When they come ashore,
With their small light ships,
They lay the fish on the beach,
Which they then haul into heaps:
This gives the seaman joy,
If the fish still has breath!
But it does not live long.

When the fish is then sold,
They lay it in their bins.
It is brought into the city.
From youth they get used to it,
That they carry this fish:
This is two miles away,
Through dunes and wilderness.

Also, a hundred and fifty pounds,
A strong fisherman can carry:
You can well understand this,
That sweat must pour from him?
When they walk in the city,
They must satisfy their walk:
Many miles around that is.

When they draw fresh fish,
They do this with nets and horses.
The shrimp croaking is among them,
For profit, also high in value:
If no fish is caught,
They lack some money,
Which brings them to catch.

When the sea strikes fiercely,
They cannot catch fish then.
The folk indeed go to their doom,
When they then go their ways,
To catch its fish:
Where the sea is nearly full of it,
In its fury.

They care much for their village,
They would not part from it,
Even if their share could be
In another better time.
When they sail from the coast,
They fish also with pleasure,
Even if they have no rest.

The great sea also sweeps wildly,
As they sail on its waves:
Wild is also the wild beast:
So is the sea folk in their life.
Flocks is their daily work.
When they come out of church,
They mostly drink strong.

Lying is also their nature,
When they deal with your trades.
When they are joyful,
They speak many foolish words.
It seems they are free
From thievery in selling,
Although they overpromise.
Net weaving is the work,
For those who do not want to catch fish.
They also do not play very strongly,
In their reckless ways?
They go out fishing for herring.
They like whale hunting,
No matter how rough the sea may be.

Can a seaman be pious?
Why should it not be possible,
When they sail on the stream,
That they would not fear God?
Fishermen can be pious,
Though there is little appearance of it,
That their mind is pure.

When the storm rages very long,
This gives them bad times:
God the Lord does this lightly,
To lead these people to Him:
If they had understanding of this,
They lightly sailed from the shore,
To the eternal Fatherland.', 'You threw the thousand-fathom fishing line right into the middle of the great Daecheon Sea.  
Quietly, quietly, surely biting, only one bit.  
Where are you going? Can’t you hear my voice?  
Quietly, quietly, quietly, quietly,  
Pressed down in the winter squash, struggling to wiggle.  
"Quickly take a bite. Take one more bite. You go all in, I’ll hold tight."  
Sigh, oh, this is for sure a true bite. I have to bait it again and cast it again.  
“Slurrrr, as the drink goes down.”  
Quietly, quietly,  
Bite once more for the real catch.  
“Pressing down in the winter squash, struggling to wiggle, take one more bite. The fish with a front tooth missing, the Dosan fish, take it firmly.  
After flipping it over and biting hard, upon checking it over, oh, it’s a big fish. I have to bait it again and cast it again.”  
Quietly, quietly, where is the real bite? Bite the hairtail fish (NG).  
(No sound up to here)  

Ah, the hairtail fishing line, right in the middle of the great Daecheon Sea,  
Blowing this sound, blowing that sound, awakening Hanyang from sleep,  
Come to your senses, the hairtail fishing line.  
Gangnam Sea’s hairtail fish,  
This sea, this hairtail,  
Where are you going? Why not bite this fishing line? Where are you going?  
If you clash, you too hold tight, and I hold tight too.  
Where are you going? If there’s a fish with a front tooth missing,  
You hold tight, I hold tight and pull together.  
If it slowly and firmly bites,  
Dive into this fishing line. Where are you going that you don’t come?  
Sleep comes and Hanyang sleeps deeply,  
I stay up all night watching you.  
Quietly, quietly, if it bites firmly hold and give it a pull.  
Pressed down in the winter squash, struggling to wiggle,  
"Where are you going? Why don’t you bite? Bite firmly."  
Quietly, quietly,  
“Oh my, this bit firmly. You too hold tight, I too hold tight, let’s try once more. Try once more. Oh, this is for sure a true bite. Oh, this will sell well,  
I can buy rice for my family with this, make a living and have a livelihood.  
Ah, again bait it and cast again.”  
Quietly, quietly, when it bites hold tight, you hold tight, I hold tight,  
“Bite firmly. Oh, it bit again. Let’s try again. Oh, this is also a true bite.  
Oh, if I sell this, I’ll give one hundred won per bite.  
Oh, this is really, really big money made. Then cast the thousand-fathom fishing line smoothly again.”  
Quietly, quietly, suddenly appearing in this bait,  
If it suddenly strikes,  
“Bite fully, you hairtail! Hold tight again. Let’s just try. Oh, this is a true bite.  
Oh, really, oh, Hanyang is lucky.  
This is really a great luck.  
The hairtail sees it and, oh, it’s hooked.  
Oh, if I sell this, it’s done.  
The day breaks. Now, stir and throw it in.”']

Name: 39_riga_king_necklace_wreath
Representative_Docs:
['O, our golden king!  
Rich gentleman of Riga,  
True boy of Pärnu.  
Why didn’t you come to us last year  
When the rivers ran without oil?  
You stirred from the deep spring,  
You twisted from the shallow pond,  
Now you have come at just the right time!  
At the light spring,  
At the dry autumn,  
At the snowy winter,  
Now you tear off your clothes,  
Break off your neck chains,  
Take the wreath from your head!  
“O, our golden king!  
Rich gentleman of Riga,  
True boy of Pärnu,  
Give me poor gold;  
Throw away the troublesome silver.  
My master bought a press:  
My mistress the prong,  
I myself got a bit of shawl,  
Got a press from making leg ribbons,  
Got some broth from cooking soup,  
A buckle from kneading bread.”', 'Oh king, little king!  
Rich lord of Riga;  
True boy of Pärnu.  
Could the king have come last year,  
If the rivers ran without oil? –  
The springs ran with vodka –  
The village flocks in the courtyard  
The field edges withered,  
Now came the time of peace.  
Now I strip even my chest,  
From the top of my head a wreath,  
Oh king, little king,  
Rich lord of Riga,  
True boy of Pärnu.  
Give me poor gold,  
Daughter’s tin silver.  
That is not what you received,  
That is what I myself obtained.  
That is brought by my fine groom,  
That is brought by my dear wife. –  
The master brought me a pin,  
The mistress brought me a pendant;  
I bought a bead string myself,  
My wife brought a necklace,  
Got a brooch from bread kneading,  
A pin from cleaning the master’s knee,  
Beads from hay mowing too;  
The necklace from bending the bow.  
Oh king, little king,  
Give me poor gold.', 'Oh king, little king,  
Rich Saxon of Riga.  
Why didn’t you come to us last year?  
When the rivers ran without oil,  
When the old men brewed vodka.  
We brewed kvass in the cellars,  
Beat the ashes for firewood,  
Cleared the streets of mud,  
The village smelled of cumin,  
The village pastures of sulfur,  
Now you come to the white time,  
Now you come to the sad month,  
To the light spring,  
To the noisy autumn,  
To the winter snowfall.  
Now you strip off clothes,  
Break neck chains,  
Large brooches from the chest,  
Golden necklaces from the neck,  
Save the wreath from the head.  
Oh king, little king,  
Rich Saxon of Riga,  
Give me back poor gold,  
Poor gold, poor copper,  
Neither were these your shares,  
Nor were these your precious gifts,  
Nor was a fine feast brought,  
These I earned myself.  
I got the brooch from kneading bread,  
The necklace from boiling broth,  
The belt from beating the brachet,  
I bought myself a dwelling.  
Oh king, little king,  
Rich Saxon of Riga,  
What shall I offer you?  
I have one ox for plowing,  
One horse for raking,  
One cow for milking,  
One sheep in the barn,  
One pig in the sty,  
One hen on the roof,  
What shall I offer you?  
The ox I have for plowing the field,  
The horse for harrowing,  
The cow for milking the family,  
The sheep for shading the family,  
The pig for feeding the family,  
The rooster for crowing in the morning,  
The dog was outside barking.']

Name: 40_trees_spruces_birch forest_birches
Representative_Docs:
['Girls, little birds,  
Locks of hair, little tufts,  
Little bald heads, smooth ones,  
Little wreathed heads, beautiful ones,  
Do you know where you will end up  
Where you will be taken at last?  
Some will get a dry spruce forest  
Some a rare aspen forest  
Some a wet pine forest  
Some a dear birch forest  
Some a wise oak forest  
Some a flying alder forest.  
Whoever gets a dry spruce forest  
Will end up with a bad man,  
Whoever gets a wet pine forest  
Will end up with a drinking man,  
Whoever gets a dear birch forest  
Will end up with dear waistbands,  
Whoever gets a wise oak forest  
Will end up managing a farm,  
Whoever gets a rare aspen forest  
Will end up with a bad man,  
Whoever gets a flying alder forest  
Will end up begging for bread.  
Girls, little birds,  
Locks of hair, little tufts,  
Pray to your God  
That you don’t run to a drinker,  
Don’t go to a tavern-goer,  
The drinker drinks to the last drop,  
The spruce drinker drinks at the Spruce tavern,  
The birch drinker drinks at the Birch tavern.', 'Our little woodcutters  
Just like oak stumps  
Haymakers, wood haulers  
The ones who rock the whole forest  
Fir forest shooters  
I cut down wet pines  
Wet pines, dry spruces  
I leave the birches to grow  
Birch branches to keep  
Birch leaves to mourn  
Branches keep the father  
Leaves mourn the mother  
Nests the sons and daughters.', "Girls are little birds  
Necklaces are pretty  
Wreath heads are beautiful,  
Do you know where you go  
Where you head to  
Where you arrive  
Where you slide your flag?  
Some get a wet pine forest  
Some a dry spruce forest  
Some get a bad aspen forest  
Some get a dear birch forest  
Some then find a alder forest  
Some get a willow forest  
Whoever gets a wet pine forest  
Gets a drinking husband  
Whoever gets a dry spruce forest  
Gets a harsh companion,
